To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a specific and sensitive method to detect the tyrosine- phosphorylated beta-1 integrin subunits in cells transformed by tyrosine kinase oncogenes.

we have identified a novel approach to detect tyrosine phosphorylation in the beta 1-integrin subunit and we have shown that the localization of tyrosine phosphoryl- ated beta 1 integrins is altered from that of non- phosphorylated integrins.

the cytoplasmically located tyrosine-phosphate residue of the integrin beta 1 sub-unit is a target for tyrosine kinase activity and that tyrosine phosphorylation of the beta 2 integrin subunit alters its cellular localization and cytoplamic domain-binding properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the role of tyrosine phosphorylation of the integrin beta 1 subcellular localization and cytoplamsic domain binding properties of tyrosyl-phosphorylated integrins in cells transfomed by virally encoded kinases.
the role of the integrins in cell adhesion, migration and transformation.
the identification of the tyrosyl phosphorylated forms of integrins and the characterization of their subcellular localization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the anti-PYbeta 1 antibodies are specific for the tyrosine- phosphorylated beta1 integrin, and that the tyrosinephosphorylated and nonphosphorylate forms of the beta1 integrin are localized differently in the cell.

the phosphorylated beta 2 cytoplasmic tail has a different subcelluar localization from the nonphosphorlyated form and that this may be related to the binding of the p85 regulatory subunit of phosphotidylinositide-3 kinase to the beta 2 cytosolic tail.
the anti-phosphotyrosyl antibodies labeled the podosome, cell-cell boundary and the adhesion plaque in RSV transformed cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an antibody that recognizes the phosphorylated form and cytoplasmically localized form of the beta1 integrin sub-unit.
the beta 1 peptide is a substrate for tyrosine kinseases and that the beta 3 integrin cytoplasmic region is also a substrate for the tyrosine kinase.
the phosphorylation of beta 1 integrins may be important in the regulation of cell adhesion, migration, and proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tyrosine phosphorylation of beta 1 integrins may be an important event in the transformation process.
the phosphorylation of the beta1 integrin subunits is important in regulating integrin function.
tyrosine phosphorylation of the beta1 integrin subunits is a mechanism to control integrin function in transformed cells.
